asr_text: Space security news often uses one phrase for very different things: weapons in space. That phrase came into focus on September 14, 2026. U.S. Air Force Secretary Troy Mc said the United States was deploying orbital space control weapons to protect U.S. forces from hostile actions. An official U.S. Space Force article called this the first public acknowledgment that the Space Force had deployed weapons in space, but the statement did not name the systems or explain how they could attack another satellite. No target was identified. The wider term is counterspace. A 2025 U.S. Space Force framework uses that term for actions in orbit, through communication links, and on the ground. It can include physical attacks, electronic interference, and cyber operations.
